title: Summit and Rivergate
premise: Xanthe Marchetti's salvage crew is hired by her old rival, Cassian Voss, to recover a sealed strongbox from the wreck of the Rivergate—a navy transport that sank carrying the inheritance her own mother swore off decades ago. The job forces Xanthe to cross the mountain range ahead of the snows with evidence that implicates both the navy and her family name, pursued by officers who would rather the wreck stay silent. Along the way she must choose between loyalty to her crew and the truth about why her mother abandoned the fortune. In the end, Xanthe delivers the inheritance not to Voss or the navy but to the descendants the money was stolen from, trading her invisibility for a name she can finally stand behind.
about_author: Elodie Ishikawa is a former maritime archivist who spent six years cataloguing shipwreck records along the northern coast before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who live just outside the law's easy reach.

chapters.title: Cold Water Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. On a routine salvage dive off a navy-restricted wreck, Xanthe recovers an unexpected artifact—a brass plate stamped with her mother's initials—and hides it from the crew. The beat is unease: the past has surfaced, and she knows moving on won't be simple this time.

chapters.title: The Rival's Offer
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Cassian Voss appears at a harbor tavern with a contract: recover a sealed strongbox from the Rivergate before winter closes the passes. The pay would set the crew up for years. The beat is temptation laced with old resentment—Voss knows exactly which buttons to press.

chapters.title: Crew Vote
chapters.summary: POV: Tomas, the crew's engineer. He lays out the numbers honestly—the boat needs repairs they can't afford—but watches Xanthe flinch at the wreck's name. The vote passes narrowly. The beat is loyalty tested by necessity, and Tomas quietly deciding to watch his captain closer.

chapters.title: What Mother Swore Off
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe, in flashback interwoven with present. She visits her estranged aunt in Rivergate village and learns the strongbox holds the Marchetti inheritance—money her mother refused because of how it was taken. The beat is grief reframing itself as purpose; the brass plate suddenly makes sense.

chapters.title: Descent to the Wreck
chapters.summary: POV: Priya, the dive lead. The first dive on the Rivergate goes wrong when a navy patrol boat circles overhead. Priya brings up survey photos but no box, and notices fresh salvage marks that aren't theirs. The beat is dread: someone else is racing them, and it isn't only Voss.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Waits
chapters.summary: POV: Lieutenant Halloway. Aboard the patrol vessel, Halloway reviews orders to let the divers proceed—and to bury whatever they find. His loyalty to the service wars with what he witnessed years ago aboard the Rivergate. The beat is a man beginning to doubt the duty he built his life on.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Weather reports force the decision: cross the range now with the strongbox route mapped, or lose the season. Voss reveals he has a buyer waiting on the other side. The beat is commitment—Xanthe signs on fully, though she tells no one she plans to double-cross the buyer.

chapters.title: Up the Switchbacks
chapters.summary: POV: Tomas. The crew hauls gear into the high passes while Tomas patches a fractured axle and patches a fracture in the crew too—Priya suspects Xanthe is hiding something. The beat is strained camaraderie under physical strain, trust fraying at the edges.

chapters.title: The Frozen Tollhouse
chapters.summary: POV: Priya. Sheltering overnight, Priya finds navy supply manifests from twenty years ago hidden in the walls—evidence the Rivergate cargo was never listed. She confronts Xanthe privately. The beat is truth surfacing between friends, and Priya choosing to stand with her anyway.

chapters.title: Halloway's Shadow
chapters.summary: POV: Lieutenant Halloway. Ordered to intercept the crew at the pass, Halloway instead delays his own report, buying them a day. Flashback reveals he was the young officer who signed off on the theft. The beat is guilt tipping toward defection—he wants the truth out more than he fears the consequences.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. An early storm catches the crew above the treeline; they lose a sledge and nearly lose Priya. Huddled in a snow cave, Xanthe finally tells the whole story of her mother and the inheritance. The beat is vulnerability forging real trust—the crew stops being employees and becomes family.

chapters.title: Voss's Second Contract
chapters.summary: POV: Cassian Voss. Through satellite calls and hired guides, Voss learns the navy has put a quiet price on the crew's silence—and considers selling them out to cover his debts. The beat is cold calculation, but a flicker of something older: he loved Xanthe once, and it complicates everything.

chapters.title: The Pass of Names
chapters.summary: POV: Tomas. At a cairn field where travelers carve names of the lost, Xanthe finds her mother's name among them—she crossed here once, heading back empty-handed. The beat is inheritance redefined: what was passed down wasn't money but a refusal, and Xanthe must decide whether to keep it.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: POV: Priya. Navy vehicles corner the crew at a mountain depot. Halloway arrives ostensibly to arrest them, then quietly hands Xanthe documents proving the cargo was stolen wages from conscripted laborers' families. The beat is an alliance formed in defiance—duty and truth briefly pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Bridge
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Voss's guides ambush the crew at a river bridge, taking the strongbox and leaving them stranded. Xanthe realizes Voss sold them to cover himself—and that the buyer is the same officer who ordered the original theft. The beat is betrayal cutting deepest where affection once lived.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: POV: Tomas. The crew builds a raft from depot wreckage and runs the freezing river after Voss rather than wait for rescue. Tomas narrates their desperate, exhilarating descent. The beat is resolve hardened into action—they are no longer running from anything, only toward something.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Estate
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Infiltrating the estate below the snowline, Xanthe finds Voss mid-negotiation and confronts him alone. He admits he took the job hoping she'd stop running; the sale was panic, not malice. The beat is love against duty made explicit—two people who chose survival over each other, given one more chance.

chapters.title: Snows Close In
chapters.summary: POV: Lieutenant Halloway. The navy moves to seal the valley and erase all records; Halloway must choose in the open now, transmitting the stolen-wage documents to journalists before his superiors can stop him. The beat is sacrifice—he accepts arrest knowing the truth is finally loose.

chapters.title: Climax: The Strongbox Opened
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Cornered in the estate's boathouse as snow buries the roads, Xanthe opens the strongbox before the buyer can take it: inside are ledgers naming every family owed. She broadcasts the names on the estate's own radio. The beat is triumph through exposure—invisibility traded for testimony.

chapters.title: Aftermath at Rivergate
chapters.summary: POV: Priya. Weeks later, the crew returns to the village as investigations begin. Families arrive to claim what's theirs; some resent the delay of decades. Priya watches Xanthe face them without flinching. The beat is accountability accepted—not a clean ending, but an honest one.

chapters.title: What Xanthe Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Voss, awaiting trial, sends her the brass plate recovered from the wreck—her mother's, returned. Xanthe hangs it in the repaired boat's wheelhouse. The beat is reconciliation without absolution; some loves survive being chosen second.

chapters.title: Summit and Rivergate
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Spring: the crew takes a new contract—an honest one—and crosses the pass again, this time in daylight, stopping whenever they choose. Xanthe carves her own name beside her mother's at the cairn. The beat is arrival: staying is no longer the thing she fears most.
